solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable copy, its numbering matching the numbers printed in it and the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wine: various places where you can get it on account

parts.words: various places where you can get it
parts.note: bars are the many places where a drink can be bought
AC is the standard abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A wine merchant notes the various outlets where the wine can be bought on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'it' of the wordplay is the wine itself, which bars sell; 'on' places the account after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Barsac is a sweet white Bordeaux from the commune of that name in the Sauternes district.

clue.text: Hair thinner on top? It resembles tangle

parts.note: a person thinner on top is going bald, so balder
locks are a head of hair

explanation.surface: A description of someone's hair going thin on top, likened to a tangled mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tangle' looks like knotted hair, but it is a seaweed (a kind of kelp), and balderlocks is another seaweed like it.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderlocks is a brown seaweed, similar to the kelp known as tangle.

clue.text: Chat with author — it won't get you far in Geneva

definitions.text: it won't get you far in Geneva

parts.note: a rap is an informal talk or chat
pen stands for the writer, as in 'a hired pen'

explanation.surface: Chatting with a writer will get you nowhere in a Swiss city.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic hint: a tiny coin buys very little.
explanation.definitionFit: The rappen is the hundredth part of a Swiss franc, a coin too small to take a traveller far.

clue.text: Hogwash from J, Ben's contemporary

wordplay.note: 'J, Ben' is Ben Jonson listed surname-initial first; his fellow playwright Shakespeare listed the same way gives these letters

explanation.surface: Nonsense written by Ben Jonson's fellow playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue mimics a register entry, surname initial first: Jonson, Ben becomes 'J, Ben', so Shakespeare, Will is 'S, Will'.
explanation.definitionFit: Swill is pig food, and hogwash literally means swill fed to hogs as well as nonsense.

clue.text: Left in a prescribed measure, it 'helps the medicine go down'?

indicators.note: something put in another thing sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a dose is a prescribed measure of medicine
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A medicinal dose with a nod to Mary Poppins's song about sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: In Mary Poppins a spoonful of sugar helps the medicine go down; an aldose is a type of sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: An aldose is a sugar such as glucose, and the song credits sugar with making medicine easier to swallow.

clue.text: Pacino playing dad cut off junior?

indicators.note: an actor playing is performing in a new form, so the letters take a new order
cutting someone off removes them, so the named letters are taken away

parts.note: the actor's surname, taken as written
pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: Al Pacino playing a father who disinherits his son.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a film plot; dad is removed from the actor's name and the remainder rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Cion is a variant spelling of scion, an heir or offspring, so a junior member of a family.

clue.text: 'A Bentley isn't short of energy — that's crazy', according to AA guidelines

indicators.note: something crazy is wild and disordered, so the remaining letters are scrambled
being short of something means lacking it, so that letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A motoring complaint that a Bentley lacks power, framed as the Automobile Association's advice.
explanation.walkthrough: AA looks like the motoring Automobile Association given the Bentley, but here it is Alcoholics Anonymous, whose guidelines require total abstinence.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcoholics Anonymous asks members to refrain completely from drink, so following its rules means living without alcohol.

clue.text: Typical of the old crone — mine backsliding kept rings

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: kept, in the sense of possessed, is had

indicators.note: sliding back means going the wrong way, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: egg is old military slang for a mine or bomb

explanation.surface: A miner who has lapsed back into bad habits kept the rings of an old hag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rings' looks like jewellery but is the container signal; 'mine' looks like a pit but is the military slang word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hagged means haglike, having the gaunt, haggard look associated with an old crone.

clue.text: Firebrand so put out when hemmed in by lower house of Congress

indicators.note: being hemmed in means surrounded on all sides, so these letters sit inside the other piece

parts.note: HR stands for the House of Representatives

indicators.note: put out suggests disturbed or displaced, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A political firebrand sulks after being boxed in by the US House of Representatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' reads as annoyed; only 'out' is the signal and 'put' is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotspur is a rash, hot-headed person, after Harry Hotspur Percy in Shakespeare's Henry IV.

clue.text: Ahriman's equivalent? Take in what's thrown in fury

indicators.note: taking something in means admitting it inside, so that letter goes within the phrase

parts.note: in a rage, a person throws a fit
R, from Latin recipe, is the prescription abbreviation for take

explanation.surface: A question about a Zoroastrian demon, then a command to absorb something hurled in anger.
explanation.walkthrough: Ahriman is the evil spirit of Zoroastrianism; the question mark allows a demon from another tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: An afrit is a powerful evil demon of Arabian mythology, a counterpart of the Persian spirit of evil.

clue.text: Such numerals pre-dated Arabic ones — ready with counter?

parts.note: go means ready, as in 'all systems go'
a bar is the counter in a pub

explanation.surface: A history note on early numerals, then a quip about being ready at the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' hints at counting and numbers, but it is the pub counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gobar numerals were an early Western Arabic form of digits, forerunners of the modern figures.

clue.text: Rival, draining (no gent), irritated

indicators.note: 'no' says the following word is absent, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: emulgent is a medical word meaning draining, used of the renal veins
taken as written
to eat at someone is to irritate them, so ate means irritated

explanation.surface: A rival is exhausted and annoyed, with a gentleman left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Emulgent is a rare word from Chambers; take off its last four letters and add the irritated word.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate someone is to try to equal or surpass them, which is to compete with them.

clue.text: Arouse Nan, rest disturbed, digging into bones

indicators.note: something digging into another goes inside it

parts.note: bones is slang for dice

indicators.note: disturbed things are moved out of place, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Waking Grandma, whose sleep is disturbed by aching bones.
explanation.walkthrough: Dice were once carved from bone, hence the slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To disentrance is to awaken someone from a trance, rousing them to full awareness.

clue.text: Women abused law making newborn cry

definitions.note: a verb: to cry as a newborn does

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women

indicators.note: something abused is mistreated and knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Lawbreaking women make a baby cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Wawl, or waul, is a dialect verb for wailing like a cat or a newly born infant.

clue.text: Intellectual lacking in entertainment

indicators.note: lacking something means being without it, so the following word is removed

parts.note: a boffin is a clever scientist or intellectual
taken as written

explanation.surface: An intellectual who finds no fun in light entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a preposition joining 'lacking' to 'entertainment', but it is the two letters removed from the end of the intellectual.
explanation.definitionFit: A boff is slang for a hit show or line that gets a big laugh, so a piece of popular entertainment.

clue.text: I spot boulders cracked to reveal part of fossilized tree

indicators.note: cracked things break apart and the pieces fall differently, so the letters regroup

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fossil hunter splits rocks open and finds a piece of ancient tree inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lepidostrobus is the fossil cone of the extinct club-moss tree Lepidodendron.

clue.text: Meiosis affects its germination — 75% of pondlife is crawling with it

indicators.note: something crawling wriggles about, so the remaining letters squirm into a new order
three quarters of an eight-letter word keeps six letters, so the last two are dropped

parts.note: taken as written
't is the old shortened form of it, as in 'tis

explanation.surface: A biology note about cell division, then an image of pond life crawling with some organism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meiosis' also means understatement, but here it is the cell division that halves chromosome number.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplont is an organism whose body cells are diploid, so meiosis happens only when gametes form, not at spore germination.

clue.text: Drag: male dressing as lady initially

indicators.note: to dress something is to clothe it, wrapping it around the inner letters

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of those words

parts.note: the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A drag act: a man dressing up as a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drag' suggests cross-dressing in the surface, but it is the verb meaning to haul.
explanation.definitionFit: Hale is an old verb meaning to pull or haul, as in 'haled before the court'.

clue.text: Jersey that fits one poorly in a word

indicators.note: 'in' places the preceding letters inside the following word

parts.note: a mot is a word or saying, from French
a means one
poorly means unwell, or ill

explanation.surface: A jersey that fits one badly, summed up in a word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fits one poorly' looks like a fault in the garment; 'that fits' belongs to the definition and the rest builds the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A maillot is a close-fitting jersey, such as a cyclist's top, or a one-piece swimsuit.

clue.text: Insect spider decapitated and ant dismembered

indicators.note: something dismembered is pulled apart limb from limb, so the letters are reassembled
decapitating removes the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gruesome insect fight: one spider beheaded and an ant torn apart.
explanation.walkthrough: A spider is not an insect, which suits the deceptive surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A dipteran is a two-winged fly, a member of the insect order Diptera.

clue.text: On the wagon but imbibing vermouth he's vacillating

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so these letters are taken inside

parts.note: someone on the wagon is abstaining from alcohol, or dry
it is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man meant to be off the drink keeps sipping vermouth and can't make up his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin and it' is a classic British cocktail of gin and Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Dithery describes someone who dithers, unable to decide and wavering between options.

clue.text: What produces heat round one side of kitchen?

definitions.text: What produces heat round one side of kitchen?

indicators.note: 'round' places one piece around the other

parts.note: heat is passion or anger, as in 'the heat of the moment'

indicators.note: one side of a word is an end letter, here the closing one

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Asking what gives out warmth along one wall of a kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, a cooker standing along a kitchen wall, while 'heat round one side of kitchen' also builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a large kitchen cooking stove, typically fitted along one wall and giving out warmth.

clue.text: Management consultant in elegant togs

indicators.note: 'in' says the answer lies inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A smartly dressed management consultant.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Gantt was an American management consultant who devised the Gantt chart for project scheduling.

clue.text: I'll follow them tucking into liquor — a couple of doubles?

indicators.note: tucking into something puts it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: gin is a spirit
'em is the clipped form of them
I, with 'will' telling you it comes after the rest

explanation.surface: A drinker following friends who are tucking into the spirits, perhaps two double measures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubles' suggests double measures of spirits, but means look-alikes: twins.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini is the constellation and sign of the Twins, Castor and Pollux, a pair who are each other's double.

clue.text: In blue, vaguely like one who's partly so by tradition at the altar?

definitions.text: like one who's partly so by tradition at the altar?

indicators.note: something vague is loosely formed, so the letters are given a looser order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bride, traditionally wearing something blue at her wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So' refers back to 'in blue': a bride wears 'something blue', so is partly in blue; brides are traditionally of marriageable age.
explanation.definitionFit: Nubile means of marriageable age, the traditional description of a young bride.

clue.text: US interpreter of excellent quality but arsy-versy

indicators.note: arsy-versy means back to front, so the end part is moved to the start

parts.note: sterling means of excellent, genuine quality

explanation.surface: An American interpreter who is excellent but muddles things up.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsy-versy is British slang for back to front; the two halves swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingster, or linkster, is an American word for an interpreter between languages.

clue.text: Dukes in ermine, I venture

definitions.note: plural, while the answer is singular: a fist

indicators.note: 'in' says the answer is contained in the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Dukes dressed in ermine robes, the speaker ventures to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dukes' looks like peers in ermine; it is slang for fists, as in 'put up your dukes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Neive is a Scots word for a fist, and dukes is slang for the fists.

clue.text: Loose coat without opening musketeer's got up in

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top
without its opening means the first letter is missing

parts.note: Aramis is one of Dumas's Three Musketeers

explanation.surface: A musketeer has dressed up in a loose coat with no opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got up in' reads as dressed in; the musketeer loses his first letter and is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A simar is a loose robe or light jacket for women, also a bishop's cassock-like garment.

clue.text: Note passages in book when looking up 'polarizing crystal'

parts.note: N is short for note

indicators.note: looking up in a down clue reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: loci, plural of locus, are passages in a written work

explanation.surface: Someone notes passages in a book when researching polarizing crystals.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nicol, or Nicol prism, is a calcite crystal device used to produce polarized light.

clue.text: Trees akin to ash on open country

parts.note: o' is an old clipped form of on, as in 'o' nights'
a lea is open grassland or meadow

explanation.surface: Trees related to the ash growing in open countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like a link joining trees to land, but it gives the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Olea is the olive genus, in the same family, Oleaceae, as the ash.

clue.text: Note about possible pen-pal I answer in African state

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece encircles the next

parts.note: NB, nota bene, means note well
ami is French for friend, a possible pen-pal abroad
taken as written
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A note about a would-be pen friend writing back from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a single letter, but it is the two-letter NB, which surrounds the friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Namibia is a country in south-west Africa, on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Fighting subdivisions of large company

definitions.meaning: second meaning: branches or divisions of a business

explanation.surface: Combat units within a big firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a corporate battle; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms means weapons or warfare, and also the separate branches of an organization.

clue.text: Economic history analyst? I'm one, critical if misrepresented

indicators.note: misrepresented means shown falsely, so the letters are set out in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An economic historian says they become critical if their work is misrepresented.
explanation.definitionFit: Cliometrics applies statistics to history, especially economic history; a cliometrician practises it.

clue.text: Service over, left to produce Scotch cake

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: After the church service, leftovers are turned into a Scottish cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like a church service or a tennis serve; it is a branch of the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A farl is a thin Scottish or Irish oatcake or scone, cut as a quarter of a round.

clue.text: Where crown sits uneasily — with which Lear becomes a King?

wordplay.words: with which Lear becomes a King
wordplay.note: with no L and no E, Lear becomes A R, a King (R = rex)

explanation.surface: A nod to 'uneasy lies the head that wears a crown', with a riddle about King Lear.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the L and E from Lear and A R remains: 'a' plus R for rex, a king. The clue's two words of instruction spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nole is an old Shakespearean and Spenserian word for the head or top of the head, where a crown rests.

clue.text: Waverley commotion? Horse dropping dead on railway

indicators.note: dropping something lets it fall away, so the named letter goes

parts.note: a steed is a horse
D is the abbreviation for dead
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A commotion as a horse drops dead on the railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: Waverley is Sir Walter Scott's novel; the question mark marks the word as Scots, as Scott used it.
explanation.definitionFit: Steery, or steerie, is a Scots word for a stir or commotion, found in Scott's Waverley.

clue.text: E.g. campion, still lacking bit of compost inside

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the selected letter is taken out from within

parts.note: to still is to silence

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a single letter, here its first

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A gardener notes a campion growing without any compost in the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' tells you the missing letter comes from the middle of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Silene is the genus of flowering plants that includes the campions and catchflies.
